findings.title: Repository Uses Wrong Database Field Name for Bracket Ordering
findings.description: getAuctionIncrementBrackets() attempts to order by 'fromAmountMinor' which does not exist in schema. Schema defines 'sortOrder' (Int) for bracket ordering. This was introduced during the fix commits and breaks Prisma code generation.
findings.consequence: Prisma TypeScript generation fails. Bid validation cannot fetch brackets. All bid operations fail. Auction cannot proceed. System is non-functional.
findings.correction: Change line 172 from 'orderBy: { fromAmountMinor: "asc" }' to 'orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" }'. Field name must match schema: AuctionIncrementBracket.sortOrder (packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:959).

findings.title: Type Cast to 'any' Violates Strict Mode
findings.description: Transaction wrapper in repository uses 'as any' cast (line 186) instead of proper TypeScript typing. This masks type errors and violates strict mode compliance required by AGENTS.md §5.
findings.consequence: Type safety weakened. Future refactoring may accidentally call service-specific methods that don't exist on transaction context.
findings.correction: Remove 'as any' cast. Update function signature to: 'fn: (prisma: PrismaService | any) => Promise<T>' or define a protocol type for transaction context.

evidence.requirement: AGENTS.md §5 Coding standards: Avoid 'any'; explain exceptional use.
evidence.note: This is lower priority than BRACKET_FIELD_MISMATCH as the code still functions, but violates style guidelines.

summary.recommendation: Fix BRACKET_FIELD_MISMATCH (1-line change), re-run TypeScript compilation, then re-request review. Architecture is sound once field name is corrected.
